question: What did the new Austrian republic declare itself to be on the day it was founded, in November 1918?
answer: A part of Germany. On 12 November 1918 its provisional assembly declared German-Austria a democratic republic and a component of the German Republic. The Allies forbade it: the Treaty of Saint-Germain bound Austria to independence and made it drop German from its name. In 1921 unofficial votes in Tyrol and Salzburg still backed union massively.
move: An independence imposed from outside is not the same as one chosen.
reference: Treaty of Peace between the Allied and Associated Powers and Austria, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 1919, Article 88
